# FTXUI Complete Reference (llms-full.txt)



NOTE: Use `ftxui::App` (not `ScreenInteractive`), `ftxui::Cell` (not `Pixel`), and `Renderer(container, ...)` for event routing.


---

# Getting Started

This guide walks through adding FTXUI to a project, rendering a static layout, and building a small interactive application.

## 1. Add FTXUI to Your Project

::: code-group

```cmake [CMake (FetchContent)]
include(FetchContent)
FetchContent_Declare(ftxui
  GIT_REPOSITORY https://github.com/ArthurSonzogni/FTXUI
  GIT_TAG v7.0.3
)
FetchContent_MakeAvailable(ftxui)

add_executable(my_app main.cpp)
target_link_libraries(my_app PRIVATE ftxui::ftxui)
```

```cpp [Single Header]
// Download ftxui_all.hpp from the GitHub release artifacts:
#define FTXUI_IMPLEMENTATION
#include "ftxui_all.hpp"
```

```python [Bazel (MODULE.bazel)]
bazel_dep(name = "ftxui", version = "7.0.3")
```

```ini [Meson (subprojects/ftxui.wrap)]
[wrap-git]
url = https://github.com/ArthurSonzogni/FTXUI.git
revision = v7.0.3
```

```json [vcpkg (vcpkg.json)]
{
  "dependencies": ["ftxui"]
}
```

```ini [Conan (conanfile.txt)]
[requires]
ftxui/7.0.3

[generators]
CMakeDeps
CMakeToolchain
```

:::

Need more details? See the full [Installation guides](/install/).

---

## 2. Static Layout (DOM)

Build a declarative document with `hbox`, `vbox`, and pipeable decorators (`| border`, `| bold`, `| flex`):

```cpp
#include <ftxui/dom/elements.hpp>
#include <ftxui/screen/screen.hpp>

int main() {
  using namespace ftxui;

  Element title = text("FTXUI Dashboard") | bold | center;
  Element left_panel = text("Left Panel") | border;
  Element right_panel = vbox({
                            text("Main Content Area") | flex,
                            separator(),
                            text("Status: Ready") | dim,
                        })
                        | border
                        | flex;

  Element document = vbox({
      title,
      separator(),
      hbox({left_panel, right_panel}) | flex,
  });

  auto screen = Screen::Create(Dimension::Full(), Dimension::Fit(document));
  Render(screen, document);
  screen.Print();
}
```

---

## 3. Adding Interactivity (Component)

Wrap plain C++ state with components like `Menu`, `Input`, and `Button`, and run them inside `App`:

```cpp
#include <ftxui/component/app.hpp>
#include <ftxui/component/component.hpp>
#include <ftxui/dom/elements.hpp>

int main() {
  using namespace ftxui;

  std::vector<std::string> entries = {"Dashboard", "Settings", "Logs"};
  int selected = 0;

  auto menu = Menu(&entries, &selected) | border;

  auto app = App::TerminalOutput();
  app.Loop(menu);
}
```


---

## 4. Composing Layout, Shortcuts, and Modals

Combine a `Container` (for event/focus routing) with `Renderer(container, ...)` (for custom layout) and `CatchEvent` (for keyboard shortcuts):

```cpp
#include <ftxui/component/app.hpp>
#include <ftxui/component/component.hpp>
#include <ftxui/dom/elements.hpp>

int main() {
  using namespace ftxui;

  auto app = App::Fullscreen();
  std::string name;
  bool show_about = false;

  auto input = Input(&name, "Enter your name...");
  auto about_btn = Button("About", [&] { show_about = true; });
  auto quit_btn = Button("Quit", app.ExitLoopClosure());

  auto buttons = Container::Horizontal({about_btn, quit_btn});
  auto controls = Container::Vertical({input, buttons});

  auto main_ui = Renderer(controls, [&] {
    auto greeting =
        text("Hello " + (name.empty() ? "FTXUI" : name) + "!") | bold | hcenter;
    auto input_row = hbox({text(" Name: "), input->Render()});
    auto button_row = hbox({about_btn->Render(), quit_btn->Render()}) | hcenter;

    return vbox({
               greeting,
               separator(),
               input_row,
               separator(),
               button_row,
           })
           | border
           | center;
  });

  auto modal = Button("Close (Esc)", [&] { show_about = false; })
               | border
               | clear_under;

  auto root = main_ui
              | Modal(modal, &show_about)
              | CatchEvent([&](Event e) {
                  if (show_about && e == Event::Escape) {
                    show_about = false;
                    return true;
                  }
                  return false;
                });

  app.Loop(root);
}
```

# Mental Model

FTXUI is built around a few core ideas. Knowing them upfront makes the API much easier to use.

## 1. Three Layered Modules

FTXUI is split into three modules that build on each other (`screen → dom → component`):

- **`ftxui/screen`** ([guide](/guide/screen), [API](/api/screen)): low-level 2D grid of styled cells (`Screen`, `Surface`, `Cell`, `Color`, `Box`).
- **`ftxui/dom`** ([guide](/guide/dom), [API](/api/dom)): stateless layout tree (`Element`, `hbox`, `vbox`, `border`, `table`, `canvas`, `Render()`).
- **`ftxui/component`** ([guide](/guide/component), [API](/api/component)): interactive widgets and event loop (`Component`, `Button`, `Input`, `Menu`, `Container`, `App`).

You can also use the umbrella target (`ftxui::ftxui` in CMake, `@ftxui//:ftxui` in Bazel, `#include <ftxui/ftxui.hpp>`) to include all three at once.

## 2. Elements vs. Components

| | **Element** (`ftxui/dom`) | **Component** (`ftxui/component`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Lifetime** | Ephemeral, rebuilt every frame | Persistent, created once before `app.Loop(...)` |
| **State** | Stateless value tree | Holds focus state and references to your C++ state |
| **Input** | Does not receive events | Handles keyboard and mouse `Event`s via `OnEvent` |
| **Examples** | `text`, `hbox`, `vbox`, `border`, `gauge`, `table`, `canvas` | `Button`, `Input`, `Menu`, `Slider`, `Modal`, `Window`, `Container` |

Your UI is a function of your C++ state. Instead of mutating a widget's label in place, you update plain C++ variables (`std::string`, `int`, `bool`, `std::vector`) and let `Render()` build a fresh `Element` tree on the next frame.

## 3. Event Tree vs. Visual Layout Tree

In FTXUI, **event/focus routing** and **visual layout** are intentionally separate:

- **Containers** (`Container::Vertical`, `Container::Horizontal`, `Container::Tab`, `Container::Stacked`) define the **event & focus tree** (which child receives keyboard input, and how arrow keys / `Tab` move focus).
- **`Renderer(container, [&] { ... })`** defines the **visual layout** while forwarding all events to `container`.

::: danger Common Pitfall
Calling `child->Render()` inside `Renderer([&] { ... })` **without** passing the child (or a container holding all children) as the first argument means keyboard and mouse events will **never** reach those children!
:::

```cpp
// WRONG: `input` and `button` are drawn, but never receive events!
auto ui = Renderer([&] {
  return vbox({input->Render(), button->Render()});
});

// RIGHT: `container` routes events & focus; `Renderer` controls layout.
auto container = Container::Vertical({input, button});
auto ui = Renderer(container, [&] {
  return vbox({
      text("Login") | bold | hcenter,
      separator(),
      input->Render(),
      button->Render(),
  }) | border;
});
```

Notice that you do not have to call `container->Render()` inside the lambda. Calling each child's `->Render()` lets you arrange them in any layout (`vbox`, `hbox`, `window`, `gridbox`, etc.).

## 4. The Frame Lifecycle

```text
  Terminal input / App::Post / RequestAnimationFrame
                     │
                     ▼
        root_component->OnEvent(event)
        (mutates your plain C++ state)
                     │
                     ▼
        Element tree = root_component->Render()
        (fresh stateless DOM tree from state)
                     │
                     ▼
        Render(screen, tree) → diff → terminal
```

- FTXUI only redraws when an event arrives or an animation frame is requested.
- Screen output is **diffed** against the previous frame and wrapped in synchronized updates (DEC mode 2026) to prevent flicker and tearing.

## 5. Choosing an `App` Mode

| Factory | Behavior | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `App::Fullscreen()` | Uses the alternate screen buffer (full terminal size, restored on exit). | Full-screen TUIs (dashboards, editors, file managers) |
| `App::TerminalOutput()` | Draws inline below previous shell output; supports `PrintAbove()`. | Interactive CLIs, prompts, progress/log tools |
| `App::FitComponent()` | Sizes itself to the component's minimum width and height. | Compact embedded widgets and quick prompts |
| `App::FixedSize(w, h)` | Fixed width and height. | Tests and fixed-layout displays |


---

# Cookbook

Common patterns for building applications with FTXUI.

## 1. Background Threads & Live Updates

Never mutate UI state from a background thread directly while `App::Loop()` is rendering. Instead, use `App::Post()` (thread-safe) to run state updates on the main loop thread, and `App::RequestAnimationFrame()` to schedule a redraw:

```cpp
#include <atomic>
#include <chrono>
#include <thread>
#include <ftxui/component/app.hpp>
#include <ftxui/component/component.hpp>
#include <ftxui/dom/elements.hpp>

int main() {
  using namespace ftxui;

  auto app = App::Fullscreen();
  int progress = 0;

  auto ui = Renderer([&] {
    auto label = text("Downloading: " + std::to_string(progress) + "%");
    auto bar = gauge(progress / 100.f);
    return vbox({label, bar})
           | border
           | center;
  });

  std::atomic<bool> running = true;
  std::thread worker([&] {
    while (running && progress < 100) {
      std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(50));
      app.Post([&] { progress++; });
      app.RequestAnimationFrame();
    }
  });

  app.Loop(ui);
  running = false;
  worker.join();
}
```

## 2. Dynamic Lists of Components

When a `std::vector` of items grows or shrinks, rebuild the container's children with `DetachAllChildren()` and `Add(...)` (always on the main loop thread, e.g. inside a button callback or `app.Post`):

```cpp
std::vector<std::string> items = {"Item 1", "Item 2"};
auto list_container = Container::Vertical({});

auto rebuild_list = [&] {
  list_container->DetachAllChildren();
  for (size_t i = 0; i < items.size(); ++i) {
    auto item_button = Button(items[i], [&, i] {
      items.erase(items.begin() + static_cast<ptrdiff_t>(i));
      // Defer rebuild so we don't destroy the button while its callback runs.
      app.Post(rebuild_list);
    });
    list_container->Add(item_button);
  }
};
rebuild_list();
```

## 3. Scrollable Pane with Mouse Wheel

`vscroll_indicator` is a passive visual indicator. To make a pane user-scrollable with the mouse wheel and keyboard, pair `yframe` + `vscroll_indicator` with `focusPositionRelative` and `CatchEvent`:

```cpp
float scroll_y = 0.0f;

auto pane = Renderer([&] {
  Elements lines;
  for (int i = 0; i < 100; ++i) {
    lines.push_back(text("Line " + std::to_string(i)));
  }
  return vbox(std::move(lines))
         | focusPositionRelative(0.f, scroll_y)
         | vscroll_indicator
         | yframe
         | border;
});

pane |= CatchEvent([&](Event event) {
  if (event.is_mouse()) {
    if (event.mouse().button == Mouse::WheelDown) {
      scroll_y = std::min(1.0f, scroll_y + 0.05f);
      return true;
    }
    if (event.mouse().button == Mouse::WheelUp) {
      scroll_y = std::max(0.0f, scroll_y - 0.05f);
      return true;
    }
  }
  if (event == Event::ArrowDown) {
    scroll_y = std::min(1.0f, scroll_y + 0.05f);
    return true;
  }
  if (event == Event::ArrowUp) {
    scroll_y = std::max(0.0f, scroll_y - 0.05f);
    return true;
  }
  return false;
});
```

## 4. Global Shortcuts & Custom `Ctrl+C`

Attach `CatchEvent` at the root component for global shortcuts. Return `true` to consume an event, or `false` to let it propagate to children:

```cpp
auto app = App::Fullscreen();
app.ForceHandleCtrlC(false);  // Allow your component to intercept Ctrl+C.

auto root = main_ui
            | CatchEvent([&](Event event) {
                if (event == Event::Character('q') || event == Event::CtrlC) {
                  app.Exit();
                  return true;
                }
                return false;
              });
```

## 5. Modals & Confirmation Dialogs

Wrap your main component with `Modal(dialog, &show_modal)`. Add `CatchEvent` on the dialog to dismiss on `Escape`:

```cpp
bool show_modal = false;

auto main_ui = Button("Delete item", [&] { show_modal = true; })
               | center;

auto confirm_button = Button("Confirm", [&] { show_modal = false; });
auto cancel_button = Button("Cancel", [&] { show_modal = false; });
auto modal_buttons = Container::Horizontal({
    confirm_button,
    cancel_button,
});

auto modal_layout = Renderer(modal_buttons, [&] {
  return vbox({
             text("Are you sure?") | bold,
             separator(),
             modal_buttons->Render(),
         })
         | border
         | clear_under;
});

auto modal = modal_layout
             | CatchEvent([&](Event e) {
                 if (e == Event::Escape) {
                   show_modal = false;
                   return true;
                 }
                 return false;
               });

auto root = main_ui
            | Modal(modal, &show_modal);
```

## 6. Mouse Hit-Testing & Element-Relative Coordinates

Capture an element's rendered bounding `Box` with `| reflect(box)` during `Render()`, then test clicks inside `CatchEvent`:

```cpp
Box canvas_box;
int last_x = -1;
int last_y = -1;

auto ui = Renderer([&] {
  auto label = text("Click inside me (" + std::to_string(last_x) + ", " +
                    std::to_string(last_y) + ")");
  return label
         | border
         | reflect(canvas_box);
});

ui |= CatchEvent([&](Event event) {
  if (event.is_mouse() &&
      event.mouse().button == Mouse::Left &&
      event.mouse().motion == Mouse::Pressed &&
      canvas_box.Contain(event.mouse().x, event.mouse().y)) {
    last_x = event.mouse().x - canvas_box.x_min;
    last_y = event.mouse().y - canvas_box.y_min;
    return true;
  }
  return false;
});
```

## 7. Streaming CLI Output & Launching External Editors

Use `App::TerminalOutput()` for inline CLIs, `PrintAbove()` to emit permanent scrollback lines, and `WithRestoredIO()` to temporarily hand the terminal back to an external program:

```cpp
auto app = App::TerminalOutput();

auto log_button = Button("Log line", [&] {
  app.PrintAbove(text("[info] Task completed") | color(Color::Green));
});
auto editor_button = Button("Open editor", app.WithRestoredIO([&] {
  std::system("vim notes.txt");
}));
auto quit_button = Button("Quit", app.ExitLoopClosure());

auto ui = Container::Horizontal({
    log_button,
    editor_button,
    quit_button,
});

app.Loop(ui);
```


---

# Cheat Sheet

A 1-page quick reference for everyday FTXUI development.

## Headers

```cpp
#include <ftxui/screen/screen.hpp>       // Screen, Surface, Cell, Color, Box
#include <ftxui/dom/elements.hpp>        // hbox, vbox, text, border, flex, ...
#include <ftxui/dom/table.hpp>           // Table
#include <ftxui/dom/canvas.hpp>          // Canvas
#include <ftxui/component/component.hpp> // Button, Input, Menu, Container, ...
#include <ftxui/component/app.hpp>       // App
#include <ftxui/component/loop.hpp>      // Loop (manual event loop)
```

## Layout Elements (`ftxui/dom`)

| Element | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `hbox({...})` / `vbox({...})` | Horizontal / vertical box |
| `dbox({...})` | Stacked layers (depth box; pair with `clear_under`) |
| `flexbox({...}, config)` | CSS-like wrapping layout (`hflow`, `vflow` shorthands) |
| `gridbox({ {...}, {...} })` | 2D aligned grid |
| `filler()` / `emptyElement()` | Expandable blank space / 0×0 element |
| `separator()` | Horizontal or vertical divider (`separatorLight`, `Double`, `Heavy`, `Dashed`) |
| `window(title, content)` | Bordered box with title bar |

## Decorators (chain with `|` on the left)

```cpp
auto el = text("Hello")
          | bold
          | color(Color::Cyan)
          | bgcolor(Color::Black)
          | borderRounded
          | center
          | flex;
```

| Category | Decorators |
| --- | --- |
| **Text style** | `bold`, `dim`, `italic`, `inverted`, `underlined`, `underlinedDouble`, `blink`, `strikethrough` |
| **Color** | `color(Color::Red)`, `bgcolor(Color::Blue)`, `color(LinearGradient(...))` |
| **Borders** | `border`, `borderLight`, `borderHeavy`, `borderDouble`, `borderRounded`, `borderDashed`, `borderEmpty`, `borderStyled(...)` |
| **Flex & Size** | `flex`, `flex_grow`, `flex_shrink`, `xflex`, `yflex`, `notflex`, `size(WIDTH, EQUAL, 20)` (`LESS_THAN`, `GREATER_THAN`) |
| **Alignment** | `center`, `hcenter`, `vcenter`, `align_right` |
| **Scrolling** | `frame`, `xframe`, `yframe`, `vscroll_indicator`, `hscroll_indicator`, `focus`, `focusPositionRelative(x, y)` |
| **Utilities** | `clear_under`, `reflect(box)`, `automerge`, `hyperlink(url)` |

## Interactive Components (`ftxui/component`)

| Component | Typical Usage |
| --- | --- |
| `Button` | `auto btn = Button("Click", [&] { ... });` |
| `Input` | `auto in = Input(&str, "placeholder");` |
| `Checkbox` | `auto cb = Checkbox("Enable", &flag);` |
| `Menu` | `auto m = Menu(&entries, &selected);` |
| `Radiobox` | `auto rb = Radiobox(&entries, &selected);` |
| `Dropdown` | `auto dd = Dropdown(&entries, &selected);` |
| `Toggle` | `auto tg = Toggle(&entries, &selected);` |
| `Slider` | `auto sl = Slider("Volume:", &val, 0, 100, 5);` |
| `Collapsible` | `auto col = Collapsible("Details", child);` |
| `Modal` | `auto ui = main \| Modal(dialog, &show);` |
| `Window` | `auto win = Window({.inner = child, .title = "Title"});` |
| `ResizableSplit` | `ResizableSplitLeft(left, right, &size)` (`Right`, `Top`, `Bottom`) |
| `Container` | `Container::Vertical({...})`, `Horizontal`, `Tab({...}, &idx)`, `Stacked` |
| `Renderer` | `Renderer(container, [&] { return vbox({...}); })` |
| `CatchEvent` | `comp \| CatchEvent([&](Event e) { return false; })` |
| `Maybe` | `comp \| Maybe(&visible)` |
| `Hoverable` | `comp \| Hoverable(&hovered)` |

## Common Events (`ftxui::Event`)

| Keys | Event |
| --- | --- |
| Printable char | `Event::Character('q')`, `event.is_character()`, `event.character()` |
| Arrows | `Event::ArrowUp`, `ArrowDown`, `ArrowLeft`, `ArrowRight` (`*Ctrl`, `*Alt`) |
| Navigation | `Event::Tab`, `TabReverse`, `Home`, `End`, `PageUp`, `PageDown` |
| Editing | `Event::Return`, `Escape`, `Backspace`, `Delete`, `Insert` |
| Control | `Event::CtrlC`, `CtrlD`, `CtrlA`..`CtrlZ`, `AltA`..`AltZ`, `F1`..`F12` |
| Mouse | `event.is_mouse()`, `event.mouse().button` (`Mouse::Left`, `WheelUp`, `WheelDown`), `event.mouse().motion` (`Pressed`, `Released`, `Moved`), `x`, `y` |

## `App` Lifecycle

```cpp
auto app = App::Fullscreen();      // or TerminalOutput(), FitComponent(), FixedSize(w, h)
app.Loop(root_component);          // Blocking main loop
app.Exit();                        // Exit loop (or app.ExitLoopClosure())
app.Post([&] { /* state */ });     // Thread-safe callback on main loop thread
app.RequestAnimationFrame();       // Schedule a redraw
app.PrintAbove(element);           // Permanent scrollback output (TerminalOutput mode)
app.WithRestoredIO([&] { ... });   // Suspend raw mode to run external CLI/editor
```


---

# Events, Focus & Mouse

How FTXUI routes keyboard events, moves focus between components, and handles mouse input.

## How Events Travel Through the Tree

When a key press, mouse action, or resize arrives:

1. `App` delivers the `Event` to the **root component** via `root->OnEvent(event)`.
2. A container (`Container::Vertical`, `Container::Horizontal`, `Container::Tab`, `Container::Stacked`) forwards keyboard events to its **currently active child** first.
3. If the child returns `true`, the event is **consumed** and propagation stops.
4. If the child returns `false`, the container handles navigation keys itself (e.g., `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown` in `Container::Vertical`, `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight` in `Container::Horizontal`, `Tab`/`TabReverse` across focusable children).

```text
  App → root->OnEvent(e)
           │
           ▼
     active child->OnEvent(e)
       ├── returns true  → done (event consumed)
       └── returns false → container handles navigation / bubbles up
```

## Intercepting Events with `CatchEvent`

`CatchEvent` wraps a component and inspects every `Event` **before** it reaches the inner component:

```cpp
auto app = App::Fullscreen();

auto ui = main_component
          | CatchEvent([&](Event event) {
              if (event == Event::Character('q')) {
                app.Exit();
                return true;  // Consumed: inner component won't see 'q'
              }
              return false;   // Not consumed: pass to main_component
            });
```

::: warning Global Shortcuts vs. `Input`
Because `CatchEvent` runs **before** children, catching `Event::Character('q')` at the root will prevent typing `'q'` into an `Input` box! Either:
- Use modifier keys (`Event::CtrlQ`, `Event::Escape`), or
- Check `!input->Focused()` before consuming printable characters.
:::

### Common `Event` Checks

```cpp
if (event == Event::Return) { /* Enter */ }
if (event == Event::Escape) { /* Esc */ }
if (event == Event::CtrlC)  { /* Ctrl+C */ }
if (event.is_character())   { std::string ch = event.character(); }
if (event.is_mouse())       { Mouse m = event.mouse(); }
```

## Focus & Containers

- Only components where `Focusable()` returns `true` can receive focus. `Renderer(...)` without a focusable child is not focusable.
- **`Container::Vertical` / `Container::Horizontal`** automatically track the active child index (you can also pass an explicit `int* selected` pointer to observe or control focus).
- `Container::Tab({tab0, tab1, tab2}, &tab_index)` routes events only to `children[tab_index]`. Inactive tabs do not receive events or take focus.
- **Programmatic focus:** Call `child->TakeFocus()` to move focus directly to a specific component.
- **Querying focus:** Inside a `Renderer`, call `child->Focused()` (exact leaf has focus) or `child->Active()` (child or one of its descendants has focus) to style active panes.

```cpp
auto pane = Renderer(child, [&] {
  auto border_style = child->Active() ? borderDouble : borderLight;
  return child->Render() | border_style;
});
```

## Modals & Event Isolation

`Modal(dialog, &show)` layers `dialog` on top of the main UI (via `dbox` + `clear_under`) **and** blocks all keyboard/mouse events from reaching the background while `show == true`:

```cpp
bool show_modal = false;
auto ui = main_component
          | Modal(dialog_component, &show_modal);
```

When `show_modal` becomes `false`, events immediately resume routing to `main_component`.

## Mouse Events & Hit-Testing

Mouse support is enabled automatically in `App`. A `Mouse` struct contains:

- `mouse.x`, `mouse.y`: 0-based terminal cell coordinates
- `mouse.button`: `Mouse::Left`, `Mouse::Middle`, `Mouse::Right`, `Mouse::None`, `Mouse::WheelUp`, `Mouse::WheelDown`
- `mouse.motion`: `Mouse::Pressed`, `Mouse::Released`, `Mouse::Moved`
- Modifiers: `mouse.shift`, `mouse.meta`, `mouse.control`

To detect clicks or hover on a custom region, capture its rendered rectangle with `reflect(box)` during `Render()`, then test `box.Contain(x, y)` in `OnEvent()`:

```cpp
Box card_box;
bool hovered = false;

auto card = Renderer([&] {
  auto style = hovered ? color(Color::Yellow) : color(Color::White);
  return text(" Click or hover me ")
         | style
         | borderRounded
         | reflect(card_box);
});

auto interactive_card = card
                        | CatchEvent([&](Event event) {
                            if (!event.is_mouse()) {
                              return false;
                            }
                            hovered = card_box.Contain(event.mouse().x, event.mouse().y);
                            if (hovered &&
                                event.mouse().button == Mouse::Left &&
                                event.mouse().motion == Mouse::Pressed) {
                              // Handle click
                              return true;
                            }
                            return false;
                          });
```

::: tip Built-in `Hoverable`
If you only need a hover boolean, use the built-in decorator instead of writing mouse hit-testing manually:
```cpp
bool is_hovered = false;
auto card = base_component | Hoverable(&is_hovered);
```
:::


---

# Custom Widgets (`ComponentBase` & `Node`)

Most FTXUI apps can be built by composing built-in components with `Renderer`, `Container`, and `CatchEvent`. When you need a reusable, self-contained widget or custom low-level cell drawing, you can subclass `ComponentBase` or `Node` directly.

## Custom Component (`ComponentBase`)

Subclass [`ftxui::ComponentBase`](/api/class/componentbase) when you want a stateful interactive widget with its own rendering, event handling, and focus behavior.

### Key Virtual Methods

| Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `Element OnRender()` | Return the `Element` tree for this frame (called every redraw). |
| `bool OnEvent(Event event)` | Handle keyboard/mouse input. Return `true` if consumed, `false` to let parents handle it. |
| `bool Focusable() const` | Return `true` if this widget can receive keyboard focus via `Tab` / arrow keys. |
| `void OnAnimation(animation::Params& params)` | Advance animations; call `animation::RequestAnimationFrame()` while still animating. |

### Example: A Reusable Counter Widget

```cpp
#include <ftxui/component/app.hpp>
#include <ftxui/component/component.hpp>
#include <ftxui/component/component_base.hpp>
#include <ftxui/dom/elements.hpp>
#include <memory>
#include <string>

using namespace ftxui;

class CounterWidget : public ComponentBase {
 public:
  explicit CounterWidget(int* value) : value_(value) {}

  Element OnRender() override {
    auto label = text(" Count: " + std::to_string(*value_) + " ");
    auto hint = text(" (+/- or click) ") | dim;
    auto body = hbox({label, hint});

    if (Focused()) {
      body = body | inverted;
    }

    return body
           | borderRounded
           | reflect(box_);
  }

  bool OnEvent(Event event) override {
    if (event == Event::Character('+') || event == Event::ArrowRight) {
      (*value_)++;
      return true;
    }
    if (event == Event::Character('-') || event == Event::ArrowLeft) {
      (*value_)--;
      return true;
    }
    if (event.is_mouse() && box_.Contain(event.mouse().x, event.mouse().y)) {
      if (event.mouse().button == Mouse::Left &&
          event.mouse().motion == Mouse::Pressed) {
        TakeFocus();
        (*value_)++;
        return true;
      }
      if (event.mouse().button == Mouse::WheelUp) {
        (*value_)++;
        return true;
      }
      if (event.mouse().button == Mouse::WheelDown) {
        (*value_)--;
        return true;
      }
    }
    return false;
  }

  bool Focusable() const override { return true; }

 private:
  int* value_;
  Box box_;
};

// Factory function matching FTXUI's convention:
Component Counter(int* value) {
  return Make<CounterWidget>(value);
}
```

::: tip `Make<T>(...)`
Always construct components with `ftxui::Make<MyWidget>(args...)`, which returns a `Component` (`std::shared_ptr<ComponentBase>`).
:::

### Composing Child Components Inside a Custom Component

If your custom component owns child components (e.g., an `Input` and a `Button`), register them with `Add(child)` in the constructor so `ComponentBase` wires up parent pointers and default event/focus forwarding:

```cpp
class SearchBar : public ComponentBase {
 public:
  SearchBar(std::string* query, std::function<void()> on_submit) {
    input_ = Input(query, "Search...");
    submit_ = Button("Go", std::move(on_submit));
    Add(Container::Horizontal({input_, submit_}));
  }

  Element OnRender() override {
    auto input_el = input_->Render() | flex;
    auto submit_el = submit_->Render();
    return hbox({input_el, submit_el}) | border;
  }

 private:
  Component input_;
  Component submit_;
};
```

## Custom DOM Element (`Node`)

Subclass [`ftxui::Node`](/api/class/node) when you need direct per-cell rendering onto a `Screen` (for example, a custom chart, hex viewer, or pixel shader).

### The Three Layout Passes

Every frame, [`ftxui::Render(screen, root)`](/api/dom#render) runs three passes over the `Node` tree:

1. `ComputeRequirement()` (bottom-up): set `requirement_.min_x`, `requirement_.min_y`, `requirement_.flex_grow_x`, `requirement_.flex_grow_y`, etc.
2. `SetBox(Box box)` (top-down): receive the allocated bounding box (`box_`) and assign sub-boxes to any children.
3. `Render(Screen& screen)`: draw directly into `screen.CellAt(x, y)` within `box_`.

### Example: A Custom Checkerboard Node

```cpp
#include <ftxui/dom/elements.hpp>
#include <ftxui/dom/node.hpp>
#include <ftxui/screen/screen.hpp>
#include <memory>

using namespace ftxui;

class CheckerboardNode : public Node {
 public:
  CheckerboardNode(Color a, Color b) : a_(a), b_(b) {}

  void ComputeRequirement() override {
    requirement_.min_x = 4;
    requirement_.min_y = 2;
    requirement_.flex_grow_x = 1;
    requirement_.flex_grow_y = 1;
  }

  void Render(Screen& screen) override {
    for (int y = box_.y_min; y <= box_.y_max; ++y) {
      for (int x = box_.x_min; x <= box_.x_max; ++x) {
        auto& cell = screen.CellAt(x, y);
        cell.character = " ";
        cell.background_color = ((x + y) % 2 == 0) ? a_ : b_;
      }
    }
  }

 private:
  Color a_;
  Color b_;
};

Element checkerboard(Color a, Color b) {
  return std::make_shared<CheckerboardNode>(a, b);
}
```

::: tip Performance: `screen.stencil` and `FastCellAt`
`screen.CellAt(x, y)` is already bounds- and stencil-checked (writes outside `screen.stencil` are safely ignored). For very large nodes inside a `frame`, you can skip offscreen work by iterating over `Box::Intersection(box_, screen.stencil)` and calling `screen.FastCellAt(x, y)`.
:::


---

# Troubleshooting & FAQ

Solutions to the most common build, runtime, and migration issues.

## Events Are Not Reaching My Child Components

**Symptom:** Buttons, inputs, or menus render on screen, but keyboard or mouse input does nothing.

**Cause:** You used `Renderer([&] { return child->Render(); })` without passing `child` (or a `Container` holding your children) as the first argument.

**Fix:** Always pair a `Container` with `Renderer(container, ...)`:
```cpp
auto container = Container::Vertical({input, button});
auto ui = Renderer(container, [&] {
  return vbox({input->Render(), button->Render()})
         | border;
});
```

See the [Mental Model](/guide/mental-model) guide for details.

---

## Undefined References When Linking Manually

**Symptom:** Linker errors mentioning [`ftxui::Node`](/api/class/node), [`ftxui::Screen`](/api/class/screen), or [`ftxui::Element`](/api/component#element).

**Fix:** With static libraries, link order matters (`component` depends on `dom`, which depends on `screen`):
```bash
g++ main.cpp -lftxui-component -lftxui-dom -lftxui-screen
```
With CMake, simply link `ftxui::ftxui` (or `ftxui::component`, which pulls in `dom` and `screen` transitively).

---

## MinGW Cross-Compilation on Linux (`'mutex' is not a member of 'std'`)

**Symptom:** Building with `x86_64-w64-mingw32-g++` on Debian/Ubuntu fails with `error: 'mutex' is not a member of 'std'`.

**Fix:** The default MinGW compiler on Debian/Ubuntu uses the `win32` threading model, which does not implement C++11 `<mutex>`/`<thread>`. Switch to the `posix` variant:
- In your CMake toolchain file, set `CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER` to `x86_64-w64-mingw32-g++-posix`, or
- Run `sudo update-alternatives --config x86_64-w64-mingw32-g++` and select `x86_64-w64-mingw32-g++-posix`.

---

## Windows Macro Collisions (`RGB`, `DrawText`, `min`, `max`)

**Symptom:** Strange compile errors in `<ftxui/screen/color.hpp>` or `<ftxui/dom/canvas.hpp>` after including `<windows.h>`.

**Fix:** Define `NOMINMAX` and `WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN` before including `<windows.h>` (or pass `-DNOMINMAX` in CMake). FTXUI undefines `RGB` and `DrawText` in its headers, but defining `NOMINMAX` prevents `std::min`/`std::max` conflicts.

---

## Colors, Unicode, or Mouse Not Working in a Terminal

- **Override color detection:**
  ```cpp
  Terminal::SetColorSupport(Terminal::Color::TrueColor);
  ```
- **Disable Unicode block characters / use ASCII fallbacks:**
  ```cpp
  auto quirks = Terminal::GetQuirks();
  quirks.SetComponentAscii(true);
  Terminal::SetQuirks(quirks);
  ```
- **Windows 7 / legacy consoles:** Legacy Windows `conhost` (before Windows 10) does not support Virtual Terminal escape sequences (`ENABLE_VIRTUAL_TERMINAL_PROCESSING`). Use Windows Terminal or a modern VT100-compatible terminal.

---

## Migrating from FTXUI v6 to v7

FTXUI v7 renamed three core classes for clarity (deprecated aliases remain available for backwards compatibility):

| FTXUI v6 (deprecated) | FTXUI v7 | Header |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ScreenInteractive` | `App` | `<ftxui/component/app.hpp>` |
| `Pixel` / `PixelAt()` | `Cell` / `CellAt()` | `<ftxui/screen/cell.hpp>` |
| `Image` / `DrawImage()` | `Surface` / `DrawSurface()` | `<ftxui/screen/surface.hpp>` |


---
